policy: Adjudication of labeler disagreements, written after both labelers returned and before any scored tool run. Each decision cites lines that were checked by the orchestrator. The policy is applied to every repository alike: when the protocol's criteria are not clearly met either way, the label is ambiguous and the repository is left out of the primary metrics.

rw-09-aider.label: ambiguous
evidence: aider/coders/wholefile_func_coder.py: model output is a function call that the code applies as an edit
rw-09-aider.reason: Model output selects edit functions that the code applies inside a bounded reflection loop, which reads as clause (a). Labeler B read function calls as output formatting only, and the cited evidence does not settle which reading the protocol intends, so the label is ambiguous.

rw-11-chatbot-ui.label: ambiguous
evidence: app/api/chat/tools/route.ts:81 and 153: executes each model-selected tool via fetch
app/api/chat/tools/route.ts:207: one follow-up completion, with no loop back to the model
rw-11-chatbot-ui.reason: One round of model-selected tool execution and no loop. Clause (a) asks for a loop, and tool execution is present, so the evidence is weak either way.

rw-32-fastapi.label: llm
evidence: scripts/translate.py:143 and 157: Agent('openai-chat:...') and run_sync() call an LLM provider
rw-32-fastapi.reason: A maintainer script in the repository calls an LLM provider. Protocol v1.1 clarifies that 'shipped' covers repository code outside documentation and tests. The stratum stays ordinary because it is a design-time choice; the label is evidence-based.
